name: The Stall

hlido_opinion.headline: An x402 marketplace of agent-callable data services paid in USDC with no accounts — with live usage counters on the page, and almost nothing else Hlido could read.
hlido_opinion.body: The Stall is a marketplace of AI-callable data services billed per call in USDC on Base, with no accounts and no signup. The design is coherent for agent-to-agent commerce: an agent discovers a capability, pays per call, and never registers — which is the intended shape of the x402 payment scheme, and the surface presents the right artefacts for machine consumption (an x402 manifest, an agent card, a browsable catalogue and a stats JSON endpoint). The counters are the most useful thing captured: 303 capabilities, 11,405 API calls served since 5 June 2026, and 286 capabilities actually called. That last number is the honest one, and worth reading carefully — roughly 94% of the listed capabilities have been called at least once, which is a far better ratio than most marketplaces achieve, though it says nothing about how the volume is distributed or whether the callers are third parties. **This review is thin by necessity, and the score reflects that.** The page Hlido captured is a compact landing surface of roughly 250 characters of text; no pricing detail, no capability documentation, no operator information, no terms, and no reliability or uptime data were reachable. Nothing here suggests anything is being concealed — a marketplace whose consumers are agents may reasonably put its substance in the manifest rather than in prose — but Hlido rates what it can verify, and what was verifiable was a claim set plus three counters. A capture of the catalogue, the x402 manifest and the stats endpoint would very likely move this score.

tier_rationale: FADING (58) is a confidence-limited verdict, not a judgement that the service is poor. The architecture is coherent for agent-to-agent commerce and the surface exposes the right machine-readable artefacts, with live counters (303 capabilities, 11,405 calls, 286 capabilities called) that indicate real traffic. But the captured surface was roughly 250 characters: no pricing, no capability documentation, no operator identity, no terms and no reliability data. Hlido scores what it could verify, and too little was verifiable to support a higher band. Re-review against the catalogue and manifest is warranted.
what_it_does_well: Coherent design for agent-to-agent commerce — pay-per-call in USDC on Base with no accounts
Exposes machine-readable artefacts an agent needs: x402 manifest, agent card, browsable catalogue, stats JSON
Publishes live usage counters rather than only capability counts
286 of 303 capabilities have actually been called — real usage breadth, not a shelf of dead listings
States a service-start date (5 June 2026), so the volume figure has a window attached
what_it_fails_at: The captured surface is roughly 250 characters — no pricing, capability documentation, terms or operator information was reachable
No reliability, uptime or dispute-resolution information for a service being paid per call
No breakdown of whether the 11,405 calls come from third parties or from the operator
Payment in USDC on Base narrows the audience to agents already holding crypto on that chain
Not tested hands-on by Hlido; no capability was called
best_for: Agents already operating with USDC on Base that need per-call data services without signup
Developers exploring x402 as a payment rail for agent-callable capabilities
not_recommended_for: Anyone needing documented pricing, terms or a reliability commitment before spending
Teams that cannot or will not transact in crypto
Buyers who need to know who operates a service before paying it
red_flags: No operator information, terms of service or pricing detail was reachable on the captured surface for a service that takes payment per call.
